newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack off on Labour investment comment.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack off on Labour investment comment.

text.p: Shares in Railtrack Plc dropped on Wednesday after Labour party transport spokesman Andrew Smith told the party's annual conference a Labour government would press for more investment, traders said.
The stock was down 10p at 292-1/2 by 0930 GMT, ending for the time being at last a sharp rally since it was floated on the London stock exchange in May after privatisation.
"News from the Labour conference has hit the stock," said one trader, "and after all it has had a good run."

Smith told the confernce a Labour government would use the powers of the rail regulator to bring about more investment in rail track and signalling. "We serve notice on Railtrack that things will be different under Labour," Smith said.

Railtrack shares have surged in recent months amid talk of U.S. investment interest coupled with speculation about the value of its property holdings. The partly-paid status of the stock also improved its yield performance.
At flotation the partly-paid stock was priced at 200p for investment institutions.
